## Purpose
The Rules page API, for governance rules on agents and workflows. It covers the rule-type catalog, create/read/update/delete of rules and rule categories, restoring recommended rules, per-agent rule selections (applied to the live agent), workflow rule views, the rule event log, and an LLM suggestion of which optional rules fit.

## Responsibilities
| Endpoint | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `GET /rules/types?scope=agent\|workflow` | `{types: [t.to_dict()], checkpoints: catalog.CHECKPOINTS}` |
| `GET /rules?scope=` | `{rules (each with usage {agents: n}), count}` |
| `POST /rules` (201) | `RuleCreate{type, name, description, params, enforcement, always_on=False, enabled=True, category, targets}` |
| `GET/POST /rules/categories`, `PATCH/DELETE /rules/categories/{id}` | `CategoryCreate{name, description, color="slate", icon="Tag", scope agent\|workflow\|both, rule_types, default_enforcement, default_applies}`; in an update, `""` clears a default |
| `PATCH /rules/{id}` and `DELETE /rules/{id}` | edit or delete a rule |
| `POST /rules/{id}/restore` | `seed.defaults_for(id)` then `store.replace_rule`; 404 "Only recommended rules have a default to restore." |
| `GET /rules/agents/{agent_id}` | `{rules: agent_rule_entries, selectable: selectable_rules("agent")}` |
| `PUT /rules/agents/{agent_id}` | body `{rules: [{rule_id, source="user", reason}]}`; see Key elements |
| `GET /rules/agents/{agent_id}/activity` | `{activity, recent_blocks (≤50 blocked events)}` |
| `GET /rules/workflows/{name}` | effective rules, each with `applied_by` (always, the ref's source, targeted or user) and `reason`; plus ≤100 events |
| `GET /rules/events?scope&subject_id&rule_id&outcome&include_passed&limit=100` | `{events, count}` |
| `POST /rules/suggest` | `SuggestBody{scope agent\|workflow, name, description, instructions, tier, model, tools, connectors, definition}`; builds the agent or workflow subject and calls `select.select_rules(client, scope, subject, phase="rule suggestion (<scope>)")`; a bad scope gets 400 |

## Key elements
- **`PUT /rules/agents/{id}`:**
  1. Saves the selection with `store.set_agent_rules`.
  2. Fetches the live agent and its current attachments.
  3. Runs `apply.prepare_agent(..., mode="manual")`.
  4. Patches the agent's tools, connectors (`filter_connector_refs`) and guardrails where they changed, through `agent_service.update_agent(..., skip_rules=True)`.
  5. Records the outcomes with `runtime.record`.
  6. Returns `{rules, outcomes: runtime.summarise(outcomes)}`.
  - Fix-type rules (moderation, stripping blocked tools or connectors) are applied to the live agent.
  - Block-type rules are only reported. Silently changing a person's model choice would be worse than telling them.
  - If applying fails, the selection stays saved and a warning is logged.
- **`_guard`** turns `RuleError` into 400.

## Control flow
None.

## Data, state and side effects
- The rules, categories, selections and events tables (`app/rules/store.py`).
- Mistral agent updates.

## Configuration
None.

## Interactions
- Route policy:
  - `PUT /rules/agents/*` needs rules.manage or agents.manage;
  - `/rules/suggest` accepts rules, agents or workflows manage;
  - other GETs need rules.view; other writes need rules.manage.
- Used by the Rules page, the agent detail view, and the create-agent form's "Suggest with AI".

## Error handling and edge cases
See Key elements.

## Nuances and gotchas
The `/rules/categories` routes are registered before `/rules/{rule_id}`, so "categories" is never read as a rule id.
